question:
As of June 20, 2026: In California, a CalFresh application is received on May 29, 2026 and approved on June 8, 2026. Under which ABAWD exemption criteria is the applicant screened?
A. The criteria in force on the approval date
B. No screening is required
C. Whichever favors the applicant
D. The H.R. 1 criteria
E. The pre-H.R. 1 criteria

As of July 1, 2026: In California, an ongoing CalFresh household's recertification was due in May 2026 and its new certification period starts June 1, 2026. Which ABAWD exemption criteria apply at that recertification?
A. The criteria in the county's waiver
B. The pre-H.R. 1 criteria
C. None until the next recertification
D. Both, whichever is stricter
E. The H.R. 1 criteria, because the new period starts June 1

As of July 15, 2026: In California, a household reports on June 3, 2026 that a new member joined. Under which ABAWD exemption criteria is the new member screened?
A. The H.R. 1 criteria, even if other members have not had an H.R. 1 screening
B. Whichever criteria favor the member
C. The criteria in force when the household first applied
D. No screening until the next recertification
E. The pre-H.R. 1 criteria, because the household's other members were screened under them

As of July 15, 2026: In California, a household reports on May 20, 2026 that a new member joined. Under which ABAWD exemption criteria is the new member screened?
A. No screening until the next recertification
B. The criteria in the federal statute as of that date
C. The H.R. 1 criteria
D. The pre-H.R. 1 criteria
E. Whichever criteria favor the member

As of March 15, 2026: In California, can a county assign an ABAWD countable month for March 2026?
A. Yes: the new statewide clock started January 1, 2026
B. No: no countable months may be assigned before June 1, 2026
C. Only for applicants, not ongoing households
D. Only in counties without a waiver
E. Yes: H.R. 1 took effect July 4, 2025

As of November 15, 2026: Is Alpine County, California covered by an ABAWD time limit waiver in November 2026?
A. Yes: until June 1, 2027
B. Yes: the waiver runs through October 31, 2027
C. Yes: all California counties are waived
D. No: its waiver expired October 31, 2026 and it was not included in the new waiver
E. Only for residents over 50

As of May 1, 2026: In California, a CalFresh application is received on March 28, 2026 and processed on April 3, 2026. Which noncitizen eligibility criteria apply?
A. The criteria in effect on the interview date
B. The H.R. 1 criteria, because H.R. 1 took effect July 4, 2025
C. The pre-H.R. 1 criteria
D. The H.R. 1 criteria, because it was processed after April 1
E. Whichever favor the applicant

As of June 1, 2026: In California, when do the H.R. 1 noncitizen rules first apply to an ongoing household?
A. Never; they apply only to new applicants
B. On July 4, 2025
C. Immediately on April 1, 2026, mid-period
D. At its recertification, starting with recertifications due in April 2026 (effective May 1, 2026)
E. At its next periodic report

As of July 15, 2026: In California, will a lawful permanent resident who was eligible for CalFresh before April 1, 2026 remain eligible after April 1, 2026, regardless of how they obtained that status?
A. No, unless they obtained status through employment
B. No, they lose eligibility at the next recertification
C. Yes
D. Only if they have 40 work quarters
E. Only if they are under 18

As of July 1, 2026: In California, from June 1, 2026, may a county require a parolee to have been paroled for at least one year to receive California Food Assistance Program (CFAP) benefits?
A. Yes, one year is required
B. Only in counties without automation
C. No
D. Yes, until the next recertification
E. Yes, but only for new applicants

As of August 1, 2026: In California, a household with a student in a UC bachelor's program has a recertification due in June 2026. When does the new LPIE process apply to it?
A. Only if the student re-applies
B. June 1, 2026, mid-period
C. At its first recertification in 2027
D. Retroactively to January 1, 2026
E. For the certification period effective July 1, 2026

As of May 1, 2026: In California, when does an ongoing CalWORKs/CalFresh family first get the AB 42 exemption for higher-education grants and scholarships?
A. Only at application
B. On July 1, 2026
C. Immediately on March 1, 2026
D. Retroactively to January 1, 2026
E. At its next SAR 7 or recertification after March 1, 2026

As of August 1, 2026: In California, does the AB 320 income exemption change a benefit determination made in May 2026?
A. Yes: it applies back to January 1, 2026
B. Yes: counties must recompute all 2026 benefits
C. No: it does not apply retroactively to determinations made before July 1, 2026
D. Only for CalFresh, not CalWORKs
E. Only if the household requests it

As of February 1, 2025: Since when has California operated its CalFresh Standard Medical Deduction demonstration project?
A. October 1, 2017
B. January 1, 2024
C. October 1, 2021
D. October 1, 2025
E. July 4, 2025

As of July 1, 2026: How does California CalFresh treat Medicare Advantage supplemental benefits (such as plan reimbursements)?
A. They reduce the medical deduction dollar for dollar
B. They are counted as unearned income
C. They are counted as earned income
D. They are counted as a resource
E. They are excluded from income

As of July 1, 2026: Through when are California counties approved to operate the Early Denial Waiver?
A. September 30, 2029
B. April 30, 2026
C. October 31, 2027
D. April 30, 2029
E. June 1, 2026

As of October 15, 2025: For how long did FNS hold states harmless in Quality Control for misapplying the H.R. 1 utility allowance (LIHEAP) change?
A. One year from July 4, 2025
B. 30 days from July 4, 2025
C. There was no hold-harmless period
D. 120 days from July 4, 2025
E. Until October 1, 2026

As of November 15, 2026: A California county budget analyst asks what share of total allowable CalFresh administrative costs the counties now pay, given the federal change to administrative cost sharing and the state-county split in state law. What is it?
A. 25 percent
B. 30 percent
C. 22.5 percent
D. 15 percent
E. 52.5 percent

As of August 15, 2026: In California, what share of total allowable CalFresh administrative costs does the state (not the counties) pay in this month?
A. 22.5 percent
B. 52.5 percent
C. 35 percent
D. 70 percent
E. 50 percent

As of March 1, 2026: A state's FFY 2025 payment error rate was 14 percent and its FFY 2026 rate is not yet known. Under H.R. 1 as summarized for California counties, when does that state's benefit cost match begin, based on its FFY 2025 rate?
A. FFY 2029, because 14 percent times 1.5 is at least 20 percent
B. Never, because the rate is above 10 percent
C. FFY 2028, like every other state
D. FFY 2027, when the administrative share also changes
E. FFY 2030, because the rate is above 10 percent

As of March 1, 2026: Which fiscal year's payment error rate sets a state's benefit cost match for FFY 2030?
A. FFY 2028
B. FFY 2025 or FFY 2026, at the state's choice
C. FFY 2029
D. FFY 2027
E. FFY 2030

As of November 1, 2025: A community partner asks whether CalFresh Healthy Living (SNAP-Ed) still has federal funding this month. Under H.R. 1, what is the case?
A. No: funding sunset at the end of FFY 2025, September 30, 2025
B. Yes: the Act cut it to 25 percent federal funding
C. Yes: it runs until FFY 2028, when the cost share begins
D. Yes, but only through the four State Implementing Agencies
E. No: funding ended on July 4, 2025, when the Act was signed

As of July 14, 2025: What is California's Standard Utility Allowance Subsidy (SUAS)?
A. A state-funded payment limited to elderly or disabled households
B. The heating and cooling SUA value for households that pay utilities
C. A one-time energy payment issued only in disasters
D. An annual $20.01 LIHEAP payment so that every CalFresh household can claim the SUA
E. A monthly $20.01 credit added to the shelter deduction

As of July 14, 2025: Under H.R. 1, how are benefit amounts capped for very large households?
A. There is no cap; each additional member adds the same increment
B. Households of six or more are capped at 150 percent of the household-of-four amount
C. Households of nine or more are capped at 200 percent of the Thrifty Food Plan for a household of four
D. Households of nine or more receive the household-of-eight maximum
E. Households of eight or more are capped at the maximum allotment for seven

As of April 1, 2026: Under H.R. 1, what is the earliest date the next Thrifty Food Plan re-evaluation may occur, and what condition applies to it?
A. No earlier than October 1, 2027, and it must be cost neutral
B. October 1, 2026, with no limit on increases
C. Every five years from 2022, as before the Act
D. October 1, 2025, and it must be cost neutral
E. No earlier than October 1, 2027, with increases capped at inflation

As of June 15, 2026: A CalFresh household includes a refugee who lost eligibility under H.R. 1. How are the refugee's financial resources treated?
A. Excluded for 12 months, then included
B. Counted at half value
C. Excluded entirely, since the refugee is no longer eligible
D. Included only if the refugee is the head of household
E. Still included in the household's eligibility and benefit determinations

As of July 14, 2025: Under H.R. 1, on what basis may an area still be waived from the ABAWD time limit?
A. Only a lack of sufficient jobs
B. An unemployment rate 20 percent above the national rate
C. An unemployment rate above 10 percent or a lack of sufficient jobs
D. Any area a state designates, up to 12 percent of its caseload
E. Only an unemployment rate above 10 percent

As of November 1, 2026: A two-person California CalFresh household (both members under 60, neither disabled) has $1,500 a month in gross earnings and no other income. It pays $1,200 rent and pays for heating separately, so it gets the SUA. What is its monthly CalFresh benefit?
A. $407
B. $562
C. $471
D. $267
E. $497

category: combine: CA elderly shelter deduction FFY2027
question:
As of November 1, 2026: Same as a two-person California household with $1,500 a month in gross earnings, $1,200 rent and the SUA, except that one member is 62. What is its monthly CalFresh benefit?
A. $25
B. $306
C. $562 (the maximum: the shelter deduction is not capped, so net income is $0)
D. $497
E. $471

As of December 1, 2026: A two-person household in California qualifies for only the minimum benefit. What is the minimum monthly allotment for this month?
A. $31
B. $0 (two-person households have no minimum)
C. $23
D. $25
E. $24

As of December 1, 2026: A homeless California CalFresh household that is not receiving free shelter gets the homeless shelter deduction. How much is it this month?
A. $769
B. $190.30
C. $143
D. $198.99
E. $205.66

As of November 1, 2026: A household subject to the resource limit (not categorically eligible) includes a 61-year-old and has $4,600 in countable resources. Does it pass the resource limit this month?
A. No: the limit is $3,000 because the member is under 65
B. Yes: there is no resource limit for elderly households
C. Yes: the limit for households with a member 60 or older is $4,750
D. No: the limit is $4,250
E. No: the limit is $4,500

As of November 1, 2026: In California, what amount of lottery or gambling winnings counts as substantial winnings this month?
A. $3,000
B. $4,750
C. $3,500
D. $5,000
E. $4,500

category: apply: CA maximum allotment large household
question:
As of November 1, 2026: What is the maximum monthly CalFresh allotment for a nine-person household this month?
A. $2,046
B. $1,841
C. $2,066
D. $2,059
E. $3,887

As of November 1, 2026: A California household's rent includes heating and cooling, but it pays separately for electricity and water. Which utility allowance does it get this month, and how much is it?
A. The SUA, $686
B. None, because heating is included in the rent
C. The LUA, $176
D. The LUA, $170
E. The TUA, $21

category: apply: CA gross income test BBCE
question:
As of November 1, 2026: A four-person California household (no elderly or disabled members) is eligible under Modified/Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility and has $5,300 a month in gross income. How does it fare on the gross income standard that applies to it?
A. It passes: the BBCE standard for four is $5,500 (200 percent of poverty)
B. It fails: the gross limit for four is $3,575 (130 percent of poverty)
C. It fails: net income limit for four is $2,750
D. It fails: the gross limit for four is $4,538 (165 percent of poverty)
E. It passes: BBCE households have no gross income standard

As of November 1, 2026: A three-person California household's income rises mid-period above its income reporting threshold (IRT). How is the IRT set, and when must the household report?
A. At 130 percent of poverty; at the next SAR 7 only
B. At 165 percent of poverty; within 10 days
C. At 130 percent of the federal poverty level ($2,960 for three); within 10 days after the change is known
D. At 200 percent of poverty ($4,554 for three); within 30 days
E. At 100 percent of poverty ($2,277 for three); within 10 days

As of April 20, 2026: In California, a CalFresh application received on April 6, 2026 lists a mother who is a U.S. citizen and her husband, who was admitted as a refugee and has not become a lawful permanent resident. What must the county do?
A. Approve both, because refugees stay eligible until their first recertification
B. Approve the mother, deny the husband for ineligible noncitizen status, and send a notice saying which members were approved and which were denied
C. Approve both, because refugees are exempt from the five-year waiting period
D. Pend the application until the husband becomes a lawful permanent resident
E. Deny the whole household because one member is an ineligible noncitizen

As of May 15, 2026: In California, an ongoing CalFresh household includes an asylee who is not a lawful permanent resident. The household's next recertification is due in July 2026. Does the asylee still get CalFresh in May 2026?
A. No: asylees lost eligibility on April 1, 2026 for all households
B. Yes, permanently, because asylees are exempt from the five-year waiting period
C. Yes: for ongoing households the new rules are applied at recertification, so the asylee is reviewed at the July 2026 recertification
D. No: the county must act on the change at the household's next SAR 7
E. No: asylees lost eligibility on July 4, 2025, when H.R. 1 was signed

As of June 10, 2026: In June 2026, a California household voluntarily tells the county, mid-certification, about a change in a member's immigration status that would lower its benefits. What must the county do?
A. Discontinue the member immediately
B. Request verification within 10 days and then reduce benefits
C. Issue a no-change notice, document the report without requesting verification, and follow up at the next recertification
D. Reduce benefits with a timely notice of action
E. Refer the household for a SAVE secondary verification and suspend the member's benefits

As of June 1, 2026: Which group of lawfully present noncitizens who lost CalFresh eligibility because of H.R. 1 can get state-funded California Food Assistance Program (CFAP) benefits instead, without changing status?
A. Asylees
B. All parolees
C. Battered noncitizens
D. Refugees
E. None of them: CFAP was also narrowed by H.R. 1

As of June 1, 2026: A California CalFresh household includes a member who is ineligible because of noncitizen status under H.R. 1. How are that member's income and deductible expenses treated?
A. All of the member's income is counted and none of the expenses
B. None of the member's income is counted
C. A pro rata share of the member's income is counted, and the member's deductible expenses are prorated
D. Only the member's earned income is counted
E. All of the member's income and expenses are counted, as for an eligible member

As of June 1, 2026: When are an ineligible noncitizen household member's resources NOT included in a California CalFresh household's budget?
A. When the household is eligible under Categorical Eligibility or Modified Categorical Eligibility rules
B. Never: they are always included
C. When the member is a refugee
D. When the household has an elderly member
E. When the member's resources are under $3,000

As of May 1, 2026: A county has submitted a SAVE request to verify an applicant's immigration status, and the result is still pending. What may it do about the applicant's eligibility on the basis of immigration status in the meantime?
A. Deny the application until SAVE responds
B. Approve only expedited benefits for one month
C. Suspend benefits pending the result
D. Count the applicant as an ineligible member until SAVE responds
E. Nothing adverse: it cannot delay, deny, reduce or terminate eligibility on that basis while verification is pending

As of May 1, 2026: A household disagrees with a SAVE result that would end a member's CalFresh. The county starts a secondary SAVE. For how long must it keep the household certified pending the result?
A. Up to 30 days
B. Up to six months from the date of the original request for verification
C. It must not certify the household; benefits stop with timely notice
D. Up to 90 days from the SAVE result
E. Until the next recertification only

As of July 1, 2026: A woman admitted to the U.S. as a refugee lost CalFresh under H.R. 1. In June 2026 she adjusts to lawful permanent resident status. If she meets all other requirements, when can she get CalFresh?
A. After five years as an LPR
B. Never, because she was a refugee
C. After she has 40 qualifying work quarters
D. Only after her household's next recertification
E. Immediately: refugees who become LPRs are exempt from the five-year waiting period

As of July 1, 2026: Two lawful permanent residents got their green cards through family sponsorship two years ago: a 16-year-old and her 40-year-old father, who has 12 qualifying work quarters and no disability or military connection. Neither entered on a humanitarian status. Who can get CalFresh now?
A. Both: H.R. 1 made all LPRs immediately eligible
B. Both, because the daughter's exemption extends to her parent
C. Neither, until five years pass
D. Only the father, because he has work quarters
E. Only the 16-year-old: LPRs under 18 are exempt from the five-year wait

As of March 15, 2026: Is the QC exclusionary period for the H.R. 1 noncitizen eligibility change still running on March 15, 2026, and why?
A. No: it ended on December 31, 2025, when ACL 25-92 was issued
B. Yes: a court's preliminary injunction extended it through April 9, 2026
C. No: it ended November 1, 2025, 120 days after enactment
D. Yes: QC never reviews noncitizen eligibility
E. Yes: it runs through April 1, 2027

As of June 1, 2026: After April 1, 2026, a Cuban national was paroled into the U.S., has not acquired any other immigration status, and has no final removal order. Can she be eligible for CalFresh under the noncitizen rules?
A. Yes: she counts as a Cuban and Haitian Entrant, one of the eligible groups
B. No: parolees are no longer eligible
C. Only if she applied before April 1, 2026
D. Only through state-funded CFAP
E. Only after she becomes an LPR and waits five years

As of June 1, 2026: A citizen of the Republic of Palau lives lawfully in California under a Compact of Free Association. After April 1, 2026, can he be eligible for CalFresh?
A. Only after five years as an LPR
B. No: only citizens, nationals and LPRs remain eligible
C. Only if he is under 18
D. Yes: COFA citizens are one of the groups H.R. 1 kept eligible
E. Only through CFAP

As of August 1, 2026: In California, a 62-year-old CalFresh applicant has no disability, no children and no other exemption. She applied in July 2026 and has been screened under the H.R. 1 criteria. Is she subject to the ABAWD time limit, and does she get the uncapped shelter deduction?
A. Yes to the time limit; the shelter deduction is capped until she turns 65
B. Yes to both: she is subject to the time limit, and as an elderly person she still gets the uncapped shelter deduction
C. No to the time limit (60 or older is exempt from work registration), yes to the uncapped shelter deduction
D. No to both
E. Yes to the time limit, but she loses the uncapped shelter deduction because she is an ABAWD

As of October 1, 2026: A California CalFresh recipient subject to the ABAWD time limit turns 65 on December 20, 2026. From when is he no longer subject to the time limit?
A. December 20, 2026
B. At his next recertification after his birthday
C. January 1, 2027
D. December 1, 2026
E. He was never subject to it after age 59

As of August 1, 2026: In California after June 1, 2026, a 30-year-old CalFresh recipient is responsible for the care of her 8-year-old son, who lives with her but is excluded from the CalFresh household. Can she get the dependent-child exemption from the ABAWD time limit?
A. Only if the child is receiving CalFresh in another household
B. Yes: the child under 14 does not need to be receiving CalFresh, including children excluded from the household
C. No: the exemption now requires a child under 6
D. No: the child must be a member of the CalFresh household
E. Only until the child turns 12

category: exception: CA ABAWD dependent child two adults
question:
As of August 1, 2026: Two parents live together in California with their only child, age 9. Both are 30 and able-bodied. After June 1, 2026, how many of them can be exempt from the ABAWD time limit because of the child?
A. Both, if each independently meets the definition of being responsible for the child's care
B. Both, but only for three months
C. Only one, chosen by the household
D. Neither: the exemption ended under H.R. 1
E. Only the parent who is the primary caregiver

As of August 1, 2026: In California after June 1, 2026, a 40-year-old applicant says verbally that she is a California Indian under the Indian Health Care Improvement Act. Nothing in the case record conflicts. What verification of the ABAWD exemption may the county require?
A. A letter from the Indian Health Service
B. Verification through CalSAWS within 10 days
C. A tribal enrollment card
D. None: self-attestation is enough; the county notes it in the case record
E. Proof of residence on a reservation

As of August 1, 2026: In California, a 35-year-old veteran applies for CalFresh in July 2026. He is able-bodied, has no children and meets no other exemption. Is he exempt from the ABAWD time limit because he is a veteran?
A. Yes: veterans are exempt from work registration
B. No: veterans were never exempt
C. No: H.R. 1 removed the veteran exemption, so on its own it no longer exempts him
D. Yes: the veteran exemption runs until October 1, 2030
E. Yes, but only if he is also experiencing homelessness

As of September 1, 2026: California's statewide ABAWD clock that began January 1, 2026: what 36-month period does it cover, and which months in it can actually be countable months?
A. January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2028; any month from January 2026
B. July 4, 2025 to July 3, 2028
C. Each person's own 36 months from their first countable month
D. January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2028; no countable months before June 1, 2026, and only after an H.R. 1 compliant screening
E. June 1, 2026 to May 31, 2029; any month from June 2026

category: date: CA ABAWD work hours reporting
question:
As of July 15, 2026: In California, a 58-year-old ongoing CalFresh recipient's next recertification is due in October 2026, so he has not yet had an H.R. 1 compliant exemption screening. In July 2026 his work hours drop to 10 a week. Must he report the drop mid-period?
A. Yes, within 10 days, and the county applies a countable month
B. No: until he is screened he only has to report if household income goes over the IRT
C. Yes: anyone 18 to 64 must report hours below 20 a week
D. No: people over 54 never have to report work hours
E. Yes, at his next SAR 7

category: apply: CA ABAWD new exemption mid-period
question:
As of September 1, 2026: A California ABAWD subject to the time limit reports mid-period that she has become pregnant. The information is not questionable. How fast must the county apply the exemption?
A. Only after medical verification is received
B. At the next recertification
C. Promptly, but no later than 10 days after receiving the report
D. Within 30 days
E. At the next SAR 7

As of September 1, 2026: A California ABAWD meets the work requirement partly through volunteer hours at a food bank. What verification is needed for those hours?
A. A letter from the county workforce board
B. Verification only if questionable
C. The hours must be verified and documented in the case record (the CF 888 form is available)
D. Self-attestation is enough, as for exemptions
E. No verification; volunteer hours do not count

As of September 1, 2026: A California ABAWD will be discontinued for failing the ABAWD work requirement. By when must the county send the CF 377.11 time limit notice?
A. No later than ten days before discontinuance
B. At least 30 days before discontinuance
C. Within 10 days after discontinuance
D. No later than the 5th day of the month
E. On the day benefits end

As of September 1, 2026: A California applicant subject to the ABAWD time limit is approved for a prorated partial month of benefits in August 2026, after her H.R. 1 screening. Does August count toward her three countable months?
A. Only half a month counts
B. No: a partial month of benefits does not count toward the 3 months
C. Only if she is in a waived county
D. Yes: any month with benefits counts
E. Yes, but only if she worked under 20 hours that month

As of July 15, 2026: In California, a noncitizen father applies for CalFresh for his two U.S.-citizen children and chooses not to include himself on the application. May the county require him to verify his own immigration status, and how is his income treated?
A. No verification, and his income is excluded entirely
B. He must verify his status, and his income is prorated
C. No verification may be required, but his income and resources are treated as available to the household
D. He must verify his status through SAVE before the children can be approved
E. The application must be denied unless he applies too

As of July 15, 2026: In California after April 1, 2026, a 12-year-old battered noncitizen who is not a citizen, national, LPR, Cuban-Haitian entrant or COFA resident applies for food benefits. What can she get?
A. CalFresh after a five-year wait
B. Neither CalFresh nor CFAP
C. Not CalFresh, but she may be eligible for state-funded CFAP
D. CalFresh, because children under 18 are exempt from the noncitizen rules
E. CalFresh, because battered noncitizens kept federal eligibility

As of July 15, 2026: In California after H.R. 1, a 15-year-old parolee (not a Cuban-Haitian entrant) applies for food benefits. Which program can he get?
A. CalFresh, because children under 18 are exempt from the five-year wait
B. CFAP, like adult parolees
C. CalFresh through TCVAP
D. CFAP after one year of parole
E. Neither CalFresh nor CFAP

category: california: CA Afghan and Ukrainian parolees
question:
As of July 15, 2026: In California, an Afghan Humanitarian Parolee who has not become an LPR loses CalFresh under H.R. 1 at recertification. Under the answer about AHPs and UHPs who lose CalFresh, is he eligible for CFAP?
A. No: AHPs and UHPs who lose CalFresh under H.R. 1 are not eligible for CFAP; they regain CalFresh if they become LPRs
B. Yes, through TCVAP
C. Yes, but only after a one-year parole period
D. Yes: all parolees qualify for CFAP
E. No, and he cannot regain CalFresh even as an LPR

As of July 15, 2026: In California after H.R. 1, an adult who has filed for a U visa as a survivor of domestic violence applies for food benefits. What may she be eligible for?
A. CalFresh, because U visa holders are qualified immigrants
B. CalFresh, as a battered noncitizen
C. CalFresh after a five-year waiting period
D. Neither program
E. CFAP (through TCVAP), not CalFresh

As of July 15, 2026: In California after H.R. 1, a noncitizen with a T visa and ORR/OTIP certification as a trafficking survivor (not an LPR) applies for food benefits. What is she eligible for?
A. CFAP through TCVAP
B. CalFresh, as a victim of trafficking
C. CFAP as a battered noncitizen
D. CalFresh after the five-year wait
E. Neither CalFresh nor CFAP

As of July 15, 2026: Mid-certification, a California county receives a SAVE result through Medi-Cal showing a CalFresh member's immigration status changed. The change would lower CalFresh benefits. Must the county act on it now?
A. Only if it would increase benefits
B. No: SAVE results from another program cannot be used for CalFresh
C. No: decreases from immigration status changes wait until recertification
D. Only if the household confirms it
E. Yes: a SAVE result is verified upon receipt, so the county acts on it whether benefits go up or down

As of July 15, 2026: Mid-period, a California household gives the county documents showing a member's noncitizen status changed, and the change would lower benefits. Must the county run SAVE to confirm it?
A. Yes, and it reduces benefits once SAVE confirms
B. Yes, within 10 days
C. No: it must not request SAVE and follows up at the next periodic report or recertification, whichever comes first
D. No, and it reduces benefits based on the documents
